question: In July 2025, which Indian state cabinet approved a bill criminalising even engagements involving minors under child marriage prevention laws?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In **July 2024/2025**, the **Karnataka State Cabinet**, led by Chief Minister **Siddaramaiah**, approved a significant amendment to the **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006**.
 
• The most landmark provision of the **Prohibition of Child Marriage (Karnataka Amendment) Bill** is that it criminalizes **engagements** involving **minors**. This is a preventive measure to stop child marriages at the very first stage of the ritual process.
 
• Under the new amendment, every child marriage performed in the state will be considered **void ab initio** (invalid from the very beginning). Previously, such marriages were often categorized as "voidable," which meant they were valid until the minor chose to legally dissolve them upon reaching adulthood.
 
• The bill grants **Child Marriage Prohibition Officers** increased powers to act on **suo motu** information to prevent ceremonies, including **engagements** and other pre-wedding rituals involving children.
